--- ## title: "Converted Presentation" format: revealjs: theme: default pagetitle: 'Sampling' slide-number: true lang: en --- # Introduction {visibility="hidden"} ## {content-align="center" style="font-size: 160%;"}
**Sampling and Estimation**
![](figs/map.jpg){height="10cm"} ![](figs/bulls-eye.jpg){height="10cm"}
## Model parameters - All models include parameters (e.g., $N$, $r$, $K$...) ::: {.incremental} - Parameters are almost never known. Why? * We usually have to sample * Animals are hard to detect ::: ::: {.fragment} - Good sampling designs yield accurate estimates of unknown parameters. ::: ## Parameters, estimates, and statistics ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'}
**Parameter**: A characteristic of a population.
::: {.fragment} **Statistic**: A characteristic of a dataset (often used to estimate a parameter). :::
::: {.fragment} | | Population parameter | Parameter estimate | |:------------------------|:----------------------:|:--------------------:| | Population size | $N_t$ | $\hat{N}_t$ | | Growth rate | $r$ | $\hat{r}$ | | Occurrence probability | $\psi$ | $\hat{\psi}$ | ::: ::: ## How do you get accurate estimates? **Properties of a good design:** ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} ::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="55%"} 1. Clearly defined objective, in terms of: * Parameter(s) that will be estimated * Population of interest * Criteria for reliability (e.g., precision) * Practical constraints (e.g., costs) ::: ::: {.column width="45%"} ::: {.incremental} 2. Replication 3. Randomization 4. Controls (in experiments) ::: ::: ::: ::: {.fragment} **Bad objective**: "Quantify the abundance of tigers in India" ::: ::: {.fragment} **Better objective**: "Obtain an unbiased estimate of tiger density on the Corbett Tiger Reserve during July 2009, with a coefficient of variation <25\% for under \$50,000." ::: ::: ## Defining the population ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'}
**Target population**
The population of interest. Should be defined in terms of time and space.
::: {.fragment} **Sampled population**
The sampled portion of the population of interest, usually defined in terms of the sample units (such as plots, quadrats, etc.). ::: ::: ## Accuracy has two components ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} 1. **Bias**: The difference between the average estimate and the true parameter. 2. **Variance**: The variability of the estimates. :::
![](figs/bulls-eye.jpg){width='60%'}
## How do we reduce variance?


::: {.fragment style="font-size: 270%; color: Royalblue;"} Huge sample size :::
## Effect of sample size ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} Suppose we want to estimate the height of white oaks on campus, and we have enough resources to repeat a survey many times.
::: {.fragment} Each point below is an estimate.
::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture-sampling_files/figure-revealjs/N-.gif){fig-align='center' width=60%} ::: ::: ::: ::: {.fragment}
The standard deviation of the sampling distribution is called the
standard error (SE)
::: ::: ## How do we reduce bias?


::: {.fragment style="font-size: 270%; color: Royalblue;"} Randomization :::
## Standard sampling designs
**Simple random sampling** ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} ::: {.columns} ::: {.column width='60%'} - All sample units have the same inclusion probability. - Easiest and most reliable method. - But not always cost effective. ::: ::: {.column width='40%'} ![](figs/designC.png) ::: ::: ::: ## Standard sampling designs
**Stratified random sampling** ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} ::: {.columns} ::: {.column width='60%'} - Useful when study area is characterized by several homogeneous regions. - Regions with higher variability should be sampled more intensively than regions with low variability. - Often more cost effective than simple random sampling. ::: ::: {.column width='40%'} ![](figs/designD.png) ::: ::: ::: ## Standard sampling designs
**Systematic sampling** ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} ::: {.columns} ::: {.column width='60%'} - Sample units are selected according to a regular, ordered scheme with the first unit being sampled randomly. - Easy to implement in the field. - Potentially dangerous because sample unit spacing could coincide with natural spacing of environmental features. ::: ::: {.column width='40%'} ![](figs/designE.png) ::: ::: ::: ## Summary
We have to estimate model parameters.
Reliable estimates require good sampling design.
Replication reduces variance.
Randomization reduces bias.

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
